authority: docs/target-spec.md: sections 2-4, migration steps 1-3, Appendix A
docs/evomir-spec.md: existing machine, allocation, frame and ABI semantics
objective: Extract the existing backend into generic machine algorithms and one AArch64 implementation, without changing any selected instruction, allocation decision, observable refusal or emitted object byte.
prerequisites: Owner reviews and commits this plan before any described baseline capture or implementation.
N01 supplies the six-unit ranking; N02 and N05 acceptance close before N03a lands. This draft is not evidence that those packages have closed.

Capture the current pre-migration backend, after first-wave integration, using the existing receipt fields for source revision and tool identities. Historical S5 objects are inputs to population selection, not substitutes for a fresh baseline.
The backend lane is exclusive: no N03b-N03f backend optimization changes are mixed into this refactor. Root serializes Cargo and the native/container lane.

inspection.registers: linscan.rs owns allocatable pools and scratch IDs; allocverify.rs separately owns call clobbers. The GPR allocation pool excludes 16/17 while the call-clobber set includes them: these are different facts, not a discrepancy to normalize.
inspection.operands: lib.rs has inst_defs/inst_uses/term_uses/term_edges/writes_flags; linscan.rs has operand_slots/term_slots. Atomic direction, optional RMW inputs, call vectors and assembly constraints require field-dependent descriptors, not only static arity.
inspection.assembly: AsmBody::read includes read-write outputs; operand_slots treats their mutable occurrence as a definition. Preserve the distinction between semantic roles and once-per-occurrence rewriting until a separate semantic defect is demonstrated.
inspection.out_of_ssa: regalloc.rs already performs parameter forwarding, critical-edge splitting, indirect union copies, cycle breaking and baseline DCE. Preserve their order and the exact discardable_computation set.
inspection.allocation: linscan.rs pin_boundaries, scan, spill insertion and frame-slot compaction currently inspect concrete MInst/MTerm. Preserve numbering, iteration order, tie breaks, fresh-register ranges and retry limits.
inspection.verification: allocverify.rs derives its own physical-register dataflow and constraints. Sharing generated target facts does not authorize sharing allocator intervals, pins, liveness conclusions or spill decisions. Its general assignment admission checks physical bank membership, not membership of the allocator pool; preserve this existing verdict boundary rather than introducing a new reserved-register rejection.
inspection.abi_frame: ArgumentCursor in linscan.rs, classification in lower.rs and frame_of in emit.rs split the existing ABI. The frame printer, condition codes and symbol/section syntax remain ISA-specific; frame layout and placement algorithms become generic.

interfaces.generic: Introduce generic block/function/allocated containers, VReg and register-class properties; MachInst exposes ordered semantic operands, occurrence rewriting, constraints, move/call/frame access views and target constructors needed by the existing algorithms. A corresponding terminator interface exposes uses, edge arguments, retargeting, indirect targets and flag-consumer adjacency. No generic opcode enum is introduced.
interfaces.facts: One descriptor supplies immutable reads/definitions and mutable occurrence traversal, with explicit read-write and rewrite roles. Dynamic operand lists remain data, not opaque callbacks that reimplement the allocator in the ISA layer.
interfaces.abi: AbiSpec supplies generated register/stack facts and the existing per-OS classification. The generic boundary/frame driver consumes locations and layout requirements. There remains one AArch64 aggregate/HFA/HVA/varargs classifier, not a second generic classifier.
interfaces.compatibility: Keep current public MInst/MTerm/MFunction/Allocated aliases or thin wrappers and allocate_for(Target, ...), out_of_ssa, verify_allocation and native compile APIs. Target, AArch64 enums, physical spelling and assembly printers are confined to the ISA adapter; generic modules cannot import them.
interfaces.independence: The generic verifier reads the same generated descriptors as allocation but retains its separate meet/transfer state analysis and refusal checks. The existing MIR interpreter remains unchanged.

steps.name: Register description and generated facts
steps.red_first: Add crates/evocc-mir/tests/target_regfile.rs: require targets/aarch64/regfile and its checked-in generated table, then compare exact ordered pools, aliases, reserved registers and separate call-clobber sets with the frozen current values. The first run fails because the description/generated interface is absent; it must not fail because a compiler/tool is unavailable.
implementation: Fix a minimal canonical line grammar in the RED; each input carries a digest of its canonical payload excluding the digest line. Generate checked-in Rust under src/isa/aarch64/ with a generated-file header; no runtime parser or new dependency.

Represent register identities, width aliases, allocatable pools, reserved scratch, partial preservation, fixed-only bindings and flags explicitly. ABI files reference named sets rather than copying their memberships.

Replace linscan/verifier/emitter register facts with generated references; preserve existing pool ordering, numeric IDs and physical spellings. Keep 16/17 and vector 30/31 unavailable to ordinary allocation, and platform register 18 explicitly reserved.
Add only the generic register/container scaffolding consumed by this extraction. Do not change allocator heuristics or broaden the available SIMD callee-save pool.
focused_reds: Duplicate register/view IDs, inconsistent alias bank and allocatable/reserved overlap reject during generation.

Call-clobbered-but-not-allocatable registers remain distinct; generated allocatable pools exclude reserved scratch. Existing fixed-assembly rejections remain unchanged; general assignment admission retains its existing bank-membership rule.
Regeneration produces no diff; the first migrated generic module has no ISA names.
steps.exit: Fresh six-unit object twins equal the pre-migration baseline; focused allocation/native tests retain their verdicts.

steps.name: Instruction descriptors and generic machine algorithms
steps.red_first: Add ordered operand/constraint conformance vectors for every current instruction and terminator family, including read-write asm, atomic direction, optional RMW operands and indirect calls. A synthetic instruction type must instantiate the same out-of-SSA, allocator and independent verifier without importing AArch64 types.
implementation: Add targets/aarch64/insts and generate the descriptor dispatch for semantic uses/defs, mutable occurrence slots, constraints, call/flags/expansion clobbers, move/frame views and exact current DCE discardability.

Move out-of-SSA, linear scan, spill insertion and allocation verification into generic modules mechanically. Keep critical/indirect edges, simultaneous copies, spill widths, constraints and selected-edge behavior unchanged.

Per-ISA constructors emit the current move, spill, argument and branch forms; descriptor implementations supply facts only. The generic code must contain the actual algorithms, not merely call an AArch64 allocation callback.
Keep selection, immediate legality, FP/atomic expansion and assembly printing in the AArch64 module. Do not rewrite lower_inst or adjust any instruction-selection rule.
focused_reds: Operand order and write traversal are stable for read-write, tied, fixed and early-clobber operands; one occurrence is not rewritten twice.
Call clobbers and alias views invalidate the same verifier state as before; forged assignments and missing reloads retain their rejection verdicts.
Parallel-copy cycles, critical edges, computed self-edges and live indirect targets preserve the existing transfer sequence.
Existing baseline DCE and private-slot treatment do not acquire new discardable operations.
steps.exit: Synthetic out-of-SSA/allocation/verifier cases pass; all existing allocation-verifier cases have unchanged verdicts; six-unit and native-corpus object identities hold.

steps.name: ABI facts, frame driver and final boundary
steps.red_first: Run the shared boundary/frame driver on a toy ABI with different register counts, register IDs and stack alignment; add current Darwin/Linux placement snapshots before extracting their tables.
implementation: Add targets/aarch64/abi-darwin, abi-linux and profile-kernel. Extract current argument/results, stack and variadic placement, preservation and profile facts; generated values reference the regfile sets.

Move shared cursor/frame/call bookkeeping to AbiSpec-driven algorithms. Preserve current private-object reuse, frame-slot order, outgoing area, alignment, save areas, frame-pointer policy and all refusal boundaries.
Retain AArch64 prologue/epilogue instructions, symbol/section syntax, relocation, TLS and system-register guard printing in the per-ISA implementation.

Finish the module-boundary test and regeneration check in the existing workspace gate. Unsupported or unmeasured Darwin ABI paths stay unsupported/unmeasured; do not correct ABI semantics inside extraction.
focused_reds: Independent integer/vector argument cursors share one stack cursor; aggregate exhaustion is not partially allocated.
Mixed FP/vector/HFA/HVA and variadic placement matches existing probes; live full-width vectors retain their current call-preservation policy.
Dynamic stack, fixed objects, spills and canary/profile options preserve frame offsets and emitted sequences.
Every generic source rejects ISA imports/names through the boundary test; per-ISA handwritten code has no duplicated migrated register, operand or ABI tables.
steps.exit: All byte identities, actual native corpus counts, ABI/verifier tests, regeneration and full-workspace gate pass.

synthetic_isa.scope: Test-only local enum with approximately twelve forms and two register classes; never a CLI target or alternate compiler/interpreter.
synthetic_isa.abi: Use small non-AArch64 register memberships, unequal per-class argument counts and toy stack alignment to expose accidental fixed constants. Define explicit reserved scratch, alias and call-clobber facts.
coverage: One shared generic implementation handles straight-line allocation, pressure/spill/reload and live-across-call values.
Parallel-copy cycle and critical-edge tests exercise out-of-SSA; a constrained form covers fixed, tied and early-clobber roles.
Frame/argument tests force both register-bank exhaustion and stack alignment.
Independent verifier rejects corrupted assignments, alias collisions and unpreserved live values; test-local expected traces check semantics without changing project interpreters.

byte_identity.input_authority: Reuse the exact sources, headers, options and target tools from tests/contracts/eqsat-size-references-20261001.json and the current six-unit N05 capture; preserve A/B and checked/unchecked identities rather than substituting a new workload. Certified g0 results remain a separately labeled regression control.
byte_identity.native_population: Use the existing Day 5 defined scalar generator (256) plus Day 7 defined memory generator (128): all 384 identities on Darwin and all 384 on sealed Linux, not a newly sampled corpus. Reuse section9_c_corpus.rs and section8_linux_profile.rs, including the explicitly requested ignored whole-corpus Linux test.
procedure: Before changing backend code, build each baseline object twice with the same source/IR, paths, options and assembler. Record existing S1 metrics and byte hashes; require baseline twin equality.

After each extraction, build corresponding candidate objects twice under the same inputs/tools and require candidate twin equality plus full-object equality against the retained baseline. Equal .text size, equal disassembly or two identical candidate builds alone are insufficient.

Use existing S1 require_identical_objects/inspect_object_size and existing native corpus execution paths. Add only a minimal pre-link object comparison hook to the corpus tests, not another benchmark runner or identity framework.
Record allocator verdicts and actual corpus executed/passed/refused counts. A test that returns early because the host toolchain or container is unavailable is NOT_RUN, never native acceptance.

Retain baseline objects only until their cross-revision comparisons close, then remove intermediates and keep compact numeric/hash receipts. Stop on any byte mismatch and isolate the first changed stage; do not normalize away metadata or claim a hidden size gain.
byte_identity.bounds: Exactly zero changed object bytes and zero changed allocation-verifier verdicts. No numerical tolerance, latency objective or performance-improvement claim. Existing compile-resource observations may be recorded, but this plan does not invent a new speed gate.

Optimization policy, cost weights, DCE eligibility and backend heuristics

acceptance: Generated files regenerate without differences; boundary and synthetic-ISA workspace tests pass.
Six original TU object identities and 384/384 Darwin plus 384/384 Linux corpus identities/executions are recorded, with no skipped lane counted as passing.
Existing three-lane MIR, random-corpus and verified-chain gates retain their meanings and pass; no interpreter adjustment or certificate bypass.
One-page notebook, compact result receipt, TODO update and measured slice disk delta; no raw captures in Git.
validation.lean: No new Lean run is introduced by N03a: Lean and registries remain unchanged. Existing project acceptance requirements still apply.
validation.current_result: NOT_RUN: this document is a plan, not implementation or acceptance evidence.

resources.time_box: Two weeks for the behavior-preserving slice; exceeding the box stops and reports rather than silently expanding scope.
resources.retention: No new target/workspace/kernel tree or VM disk. Only the bounded baseline object set needed for cross-revision comparison is retained temporarily; no full disassembly dumps. Never delete contracts, sealed fixtures, open-task evidence or Lean .lake. Record net disk change at closure.

stop_rule: Stop on any source-semantic/ABI/selection change required to continue, unexplained object-byte or verifier-verdict drift, unavailable mandatory native lane, capture cap, disk safety floor or time box. Preserve the minimal failing case and classify missing coverage honestly. A suspected pre-existing defect is separate work, not permission to change behavior inside N03a.
claim_ceiling: A behavior-preserving three-layer backend for the existing AArch64 targets on the stated test population. Neither a new target, a proved backend, an optimization gain, improved C coverage, nor completion of N07 steps 4-6.
